# TS9102

> **Reserved: not currently emitted by the compiler.** This code is catalogued, but no
> typesugar check reports it yet. If your build fails, look up the code it actually prints.

**Category:** Derive · **Severity:** Error

## Message

```
@derive({typeclass}) requires an interface, class, or type alias
```

## Explanation

The @derive decorator can only be applied to:
- interface declarations
- class declarations
- type alias declarations

It cannot be applied to:
- function declarations
- variable declarations
- other kinds of declarations

<!-- prettier-ignore-end -->
<!-- generated:end -->

## Example

`@derive` describes a type, so it goes on the declaration of one:

```typescript
/** @derive(Eq) */
function makePoint() {
  // ✗ a function, not a type
  return { x: 0, y: 0 };
}
```

Today a JSDoc `@derive` on a function is ignored with a warning ("JSDoc macro tag @derive is not supported on a function declaration and was ignored"), and on a variable it is ignored without one; neither is reported with this code yet.

## How to fix

Put `@derive` on the interface, class or type alias:

```typescript
/** @derive(Eq) */
interface Point {
  x: number;
  y: number;
}

function makePoint(): Point {
  return { x: 0, y: 0 };
}
```

A `@derive` that fails because a field's type has no instance is a different error: [TS9101](./TS9101.md). For a field type you don't own, give it an instance in a module of your own and import that module, by hand with `/** @impl Eq<External> */` or derived with `export const eqExternal = derived<Eq<External>>();`; see [Instances for types you don't own](/guides/typeclasses#external-types).
